verses.1:1: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.1:2: "I will utterly sweep away all things from the face of the earth," declares the LORD.
verses.1:3: "I will sweep away man and beast; I will sweep away the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks along with the wicked; and I will cut off mankind from the face of the earth," declares the LORD.
verses.1:4: "I will also stretch out My hand against Judah, and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, and the very name of the idolatrous priests along with the priests,
verses.1:5: and those who bow down on the housetops to the host of heaven, and those who bow down and swear oaths to the LORD, yet also swear by Milcom,
verses.1:6: and those who have turned back from following the LORD, and who have not sought the LORD nor inquired of Him."
verses.1:7: Be silent before the Lord GOD! For the day of the LORD is near; for the LORD has prepared a sacrifice, and He has consecrated His invited guests.
verses.1:8: "And it shall come to pass on the day of the LORD's sacrifice that I will punish the princes and the king's sons, and all who clothe themselves in foreign apparel.
verses.1:9: On that day I will also punish all who leap over the threshold, who fill their master's house with violence and deceit.
verses.1:10: And on that day," declares the LORD, "there shall be the sound of an outcry from the Fish Gate, a wailing from the Second Quarter, and a great crashing from the hills."
verses.1:11: Wail, O inhabitants of Maktesh! For all the merchant people are silenced; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
verses.1:12: "And it shall come to pass at that time that I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and punish the men who are settled on their dregs, who say in their heart, 'The LORD will not do good, nor will He do evil.'
verses.1:13: Therefore their wealth shall become plunder, and their houses a desolation; they shall build houses, but shall not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but shall not drink their wine."
verses.1:14: The great day of the LORD is near; it is near and hastens exceedingly. The sound of the day of the LORD is bitter; there the mighty warrior cries aloud.
verses.1:15: A day of wrath is that day—a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and deep gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,
verses.1:16: a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
verses.1:17: "And I will bring distress upon mankind, and they shall walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD; their blood shall be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung."
verses.1:18: Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the LORD; and by the fire of His jealousy the whole earth shall be consumed, for a full and sudden end He will make of all the inhabitants of the earth.
verses.2:1: Gather yourselves together, yes, gather together, O shameless nation,
verses.2:2: before the decree brings forth—the day passes away like chaff—before the fierce anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the day of the anger of the LORD comes upon you.
verses.2:3: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who have carried out His justice; seek righteousness, seek humility. Perhaps you will be hidden in the day of the anger of the LORD.
verses.2:4: For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation; they shall drive out Ashdod at noonday, and Ekron shall be uprooted.
verses.2:5: Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, the nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, O Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I will destroy you, so that no inhabitant remains."
verses.2:6: And the seacoast shall become pastures, with meadows for shepherds and folds for flocks.
verses.2:7: And the coast shall belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; upon them they shall pasture, and in the houses of Ashkelon they shall lie down at evening; for the LORD their God will visit them and restore their fortunes.
verses.2:8: "I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, with which they have reproached My people and boasted arrogantly against their territory.
verses.2:9: Therefore, as I live," declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, "surely Moab shall be like Sodom, and the children of Ammon like Gomorrah—a land possessed by nettles, and salt pits, and a desolation forever. The remnant of My people shall plunder them, and the rest of My nation shall possess them."
verses.2:10: This they shall have in return for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:11: The LORD will be awesome to them, for He will famish all the gods of the earth; and every man shall worship Him from his own place, all the coastlands of the nations.
verses.2:12: "You also, O Cushites, shall be slain by My sword."
verses.2:13: And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria, and He will make Nineveh a desolation, a dry waste like the wilderness.
verses.2:14: Herds shall lie down in her midst, every beast of the nations; both the desert owl and the bittern shall lodge on her capitals; a voice shall sing in the window; desolation shall be on the threshold, for He has laid bare her cedarwork.
verses.2:15: This is the exultant city that dwelt securely, that said in her heart, "I am, and there is none besides me." How she has become a desolation, a resting place for beasts! Everyone who passes by her shall hiss and shake his hand.
verses.3:1: Woe to her who is rebellious and defiled, to the oppressing city!
verses.3:2: She has not listened to the voice; she has not accepted correction; she has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.
verses.3:3: Her princes in her midst are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves that leave no bone until the morning.
verses.3:4: Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men; her priests have profaned what is holy; they have done violence to the law.
verses.3:5: The LORD is righteous in her midst; He will do no unrighteousness. Morning by morning He brings His justice to light; He does not fail, yet the unjust knows no shame.
verses.3:6: "I have cut off nations; their corner towers are in ruins. I have laid waste their streets, so that no one passes by. Their cities are laid desolate, without a man, without an inhabitant.
verses.3:7: I said, 'Surely you will fear Me, you will accept correction'; so that her dwelling would not be cut off, despite all that I had appointed against her. Yet they rose early and corrupted all their deeds.
verses.3:8: Therefore wait for Me," declares the LORD, "until the day I rise up for plunder; for My determination is to gather the nations, to assemble the kingdoms, to pour out upon them My indignation, all My fierce anger; for by the fire of My jealousy the whole earth shall be consumed.
verses.3:9: For then I will restore to the peoples a pure language, that all of them may call upon the name of the LORD, to serve Him with one accord.
verses.3:10: From beyond the rivers of Cush, My worshipers, the daughter of My dispersed ones, shall bring My offering.
verses.3:11: On that day you shall not be put to shame for all your deeds by which you have transgressed against Me; for then I will remove from your midst your proudly exultant ones, and you shall no longer be haughty on My holy mountain.
verses.3:12: And I will leave in your midst a humble and lowly people, and they shall take refuge in the name of the LORD."
verses.3:13: The remnant of Israel shall do no unrighteousness and speak no lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth; for they shall pasture and lie down, and no one shall make them afraid.
verses.3:14: Sing aloud, O daughter of Zion! Shout for joy, O Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, O daughter of Jerusalem!
verses.3:15: The LORD has taken away your judgments; He has cleared away your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you shall fear evil no more.
verses.3:16: On that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: "Do not fear; O Zion, do not let your hands grow weak."
verses.3:17: The LORD your God is in your midst, a Mighty One who will save; He will rejoice over you with gladness, He will quiet you in His love, He will exult over you with singing.
verses.3:18: "I will gather those who grieve over the appointed festival; they belong to you, upon whom reproach was a burden.
verses.3:19: Behold, at that time I will deal with all who afflict you; I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will make them a praise and a renown in every land where they were put to shame.
verses.3:20: At that time I will bring you home, even at the time when I gather you; for I will make you a renown and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes," says the LORD.

notes.1:5: Milcom renders Hebrew Malkam, the Ammonite deity, which can also be read as their king, denoting syncretistic oaths alongside oaths to the LORD.
notes.1:10: The Second Quarter translates Hebrew Mishneh, a newer residential district of Jerusalem.
notes.1:11: Maktesh, literally the Mortar, was a hollow commercial district of Jerusalem; the merchant people translates Hebrew people of Canaan, an idiom for traders.
notes.1:12: Settled on their dregs draws on a winemaking image of wine left undisturbed on its sediment, illustrating spiritual complacency.
notes.2:1: Shameless nation renders Hebrew lo nikhsaf, meaning either without desire for the LORD or without shame.
notes.2:4: The Hebrew employs wordplay connecting the cities with their doom: Gaza, Azzah, shall be forsaken, azuvah, and Ekron shall be uprooted, te'aqer.
notes.2:7: The Hebrew ketiv reads shevutam and the qere reads shevitam; both express the idiom of turning back captivity or restoring fortunes, rendered here following the qere.
notes.2:11: Famish reflects the vivid Hebrew verb meaning to make lean, depicting the gods of the nations deprived of worship and offerings.
notes.3:8: For plunder follows the Masoretic vocalization le'ad, meaning for prey or plunder, whereas some ancient versions read le'ed, as a witness.
notes.3:9: With one accord translates the literal Hebrew idiom with one shoulder, conveying united service.
notes.3:17: He will quiet you in His love follows the Masoretic verb yacharish, meaning to be quiet or to quiet someone, expressing serene love that stills fear.
notes.3:18: The Hebrew wording is terse, literally referring to those grieving away from the appointed festival whom the LORD gathers because reproach rested upon them as a burden.
